summary: The bad() method reads an untrusted line from a network socket and concatenates it directly into an OS command passed to Runtime.exec(), creating a CWE-78 command-injection sink. The fix validates the socket-derived data against a strict allowlist of characters that are legitimate for a filesystem path argument to `ls`/`dir` (letters, digits, and the safe path punctuation `. / _ -`) before it is ever used to build the command. Valid path arguments still flow through to exec() and the feature continues to work; only input containing shell/argument metacharacters (spaces, `;`, `&`, `|`, `$`, backticks, quotes, etc.) is rejected, which neutralizes the injection without disabling functionality or returning a constant result.
